Compare growth references child by child

Source: R/quant-condref.R
wgh_condref_compare.Rd

Fits the references on part of the children and predicts the others (child-level cross-validation, as in wgh_condref_cv()), scores every held-out prediction with wgh_score_rows(), and compares each reference with a chosen reference by paired differences with a child-level bootstrap (wgh_paired_scores()). This answers whether one reference is better than another for the same children, with an honest interval, which a comparison of average scores cannot (Book 2 Chapter 16).

Usage

wgh_condref_compare(
  panel,
  models = c("conditional", "persistence", "unconditional"),
  reference = "who",
  score = c("crps", "wis", "pinball", "abs_error"),
  by = NULL,
  folds = 5,
  formula = ~baseline_haz + baseline_baz + baseline_age,
  taus = wgh_taus(c(0.03, 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9, 0.95, 0.97)),
  B = 1000,
  seed = 2026
)

Arguments

panel

Output of wgh_conditional_panel().

models

References to compare: any of "conditional", "unconditional", "persistence", "who" and "forest" (a quantile random forest, needs ranger).

reference

The reference every model is compared with.

score

"crps", "wis", "pinball" or "abs_error" (lower is better for all).

by

Optional grouping, for example c("sex", "target_nominal").

folds

Number of child-level folds, or "site" for leave-one-site-out.

formula, taus

Passed to wgh_condref().

B

Bootstrap replicates for the paired intervals.

seed

Random seed.

Value

A tibble with one row per model (and group): the mean scores of the model and the reference, the mean paired difference with its interval, the relative change and a p-value. A negative difference means the model scores better than the reference. The out-of-fold row-level scores are attached as attribute "rows".

Examples

# \donttest{
cp <- wgh_conditional_panel(growdat, targets = c(10, 12))
wgh_condref_compare(cp, models = c("conditional", "persistence"), reference = "who",
                    folds = 3, B = 200)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 12
#>   model       reference score mean_new mean_old mean_diff  lower  upper
#>   <chr>       <chr>     <chr>    <dbl>    <dbl>     <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1 conditional who       crps     0.208    0.550    -0.343 -0.380 -0.301
#> 2 persistence who       crps     0.224    0.550    -0.326 -0.365 -0.285
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: relative_change_pct <dbl>, p_value <dbl>, n_rows <int>,
#> #   n_children <int>
# }
